notes.summary: Data Interpretation gives information as a table, bar or line graph, pie chart or a short caselet and asks a set of questions on percentages, ratios, averages and growth. IBPS and SBI Prelims carry 1 or 2 DI sets of about 5 questions each, while Mains sets are longer, often with missing data or caselets, and carry high marks.
keyPoints: Percentage change = (New − Old) ÷ Old × 100. Example: production rising from 40 to 48 is an 8 ÷ 40 = 20% increase.
'A is what percent of B' = A ÷ B × 100; 'A is what percent more than B' = (A − B) ÷ B × 100. The value after 'than' is always the base.
Pie chart in degrees: value = (sector angle ÷ 360) × total. 72° = 72/360 = 1/5 = 20%, and 1% = 3.6°.
Profit = Income − Expenditure. Profit % on expenditure = Profit ÷ Expenditure × 100: income 330 and expenditure 250 give 80 ÷ 250 = 32%.
Average = Sum ÷ Number of values. Missing value = Average × Number of values − Sum of known values.
Ratio of totals: add the columns first, then simplify. 1600 : 960 = 5 : 3.
Successive percentage changes multiply, they do not add: +10% then −20% means 1.1 × 0.8 = 0.88, a net fall of 12%.
To compare fractions such as 110/125 and 135/150, convert to decimals (0.88 and 0.90) or cross-multiply (110 × 150 = 16500 < 135 × 125 = 16875).
When answer options are far apart, approximate (for example 33.3% ≈ 1/3) instead of doing exact division.
traps: Taking the wrong base for percentage change, such as the new value or the wrong year.
Assuming the biggest absolute increase is also the biggest percentage increase; the smaller base often gives the higher percentage.
Adding successive percentage changes instead of multiplying the growth factors.
Calculating profit percentage on income when the question asks for it on expenditure, or the other way round.
Ignoring units such as thousands, lakh or crore and choosing an answer that is off by a factor of 10 or 100.
notes.examTip: Read all the questions of a set before you start, work out column totals and averages once and reuse them, and approximate whenever the options are well spread.

questions.text:
The table shows the number of laptops sold by a store.
Month | Laptops sold
January | 240
February | 310
March | 280
April | 350
May | 320
In how many months were the sales more than the average monthly sales of these five months?
questions.explanation:
Total = 240 + 310 + 280 + 350 + 320 = 1500.
Average = 1500 ÷ 5 = 300.
Months above 300: February (310), April (350) and May (320).
So the sales were above average in 3 months.

questions.text: A pie chart shows how a family spends its monthly expenditure of ₹50,000. The sector for Food has a central angle of 72°. How much does the family spend on Food each month?
questions.explanation:
The full circle of 360° stands for ₹50,000.
Food's share = 72 ÷ 360 = 1/5.
Spending on Food = 1/5 × 50,000 = ₹10,000.

questions.text:
The table shows the income and expenditure of a company (in ₹ crore).
Year | Income | Expenditure
2019 | 120 | 90
2020 | 150 | 110
2021 | 160 | 130
2022 | 180 | 135
In which year was the profit (Income − Expenditure) the highest?

The table shows the income and expenditure of a firm (in ₹ lakh).
Year | Income | Expenditure
2020 | 210 | 150
2021 | 260 | 200
2022 | 330 | 250
Profit % = (Income − Expenditure) ÷ Expenditure × 100. What was the profit percentage of the firm in 2022?
questions.explanation:
Profit in 2022 = 330 − 250 = ₹80 lakh.
Profit % = 80 ÷ 250 × 100 = 32%.
(Dividing by income instead, 80 ÷ 330, gives the wrong value 24.2%; 30% is the 2021 figure.)

questions.text:
The table shows the number of students enrolled in three courses at a coaching institute.
Year | Banking | SSC | Railways
2021 | 450 | 380 | 280
2022 | 520 | 420 | 320
2023 | 630 | 460 | 360
What is the ratio of the total Banking students to the total Railways students over the three years?

The number of two-wheelers produced by a company (in thousands) is given below.
2018: 40
2019: 48
2020: 42
2021: 56
2022: 70
In which year was the percentage increase in production over the previous year the highest?
questions.explanation:
2019: (48 − 40) ÷ 40 = 20%.
2020: production fell, so there is no increase.
2021: (56 − 42) ÷ 42 = 14 ÷ 42 ≈ 33.3%.
2022: (70 − 56) ÷ 56 = 14 ÷ 56 = 25%.
2021 and 2022 have the same absolute rise of 14, but 2021 has the smaller base, so 2021 has the highest percentage increase.

questions.text:
A company has 2,400 employees, distributed by department as follows.
HR: 10%
Sales: 30%
IT: 25%
Finance: 15%
Operations: 20%
40% of the IT employees and 25% of the Sales employees are women. How many more women work in IT than in Sales?
questions.explanation:
IT employees = 25% of 2400 = 600; women in IT = 40% of 600 = 240.
Sales employees = 30% of 2400 = 720; women in Sales = 25% of 720 = 180.
Difference = 240 − 180 = 60.

questions.text:
The average monthly sales of a shop from January to June was 450 units. The sales were:
January: 420
February: 480
March: 390
April: ?
May: 510
June: 460
What were the sales in April?
questions.explanation:
Total for 6 months = 450 × 6 = 2700.
Sum of the known months = 420 + 480 + 390 + 510 + 460 = 2260.
April = 2700 − 2260 = 440 units.

questions.text:
The table shows the exports and imports of a country (in ₹ thousand crore).
Year | Exports | Imports
2019 | 80 | 100
2020 | 90 | 120
2021 | 110 | 125
2022 | 135 | 150
In which year was the ratio of exports to imports the highest?

A bank branch opened 1,200 new accounts in a year. 40% of them were savings accounts, and the remaining accounts were current accounts and fixed-deposit accounts in the ratio 4 : 5. Senior citizens opened 20% of the fixed-deposit accounts. How many fixed-deposit accounts were opened by senior citizens?
questions.explanation:
Savings accounts = 40% of 1200 = 480, so the remaining accounts = 1200 − 480 = 720.
Fixed-deposit accounts = 720 × 5/9 = 400 (current accounts = 320).
Opened by senior citizens = 20% of 400 = 80.
(Taking 20% of the current accounts gives the wrong value 64.)

questions.text:
The sales of a company were ₹250 crore in 2020. The percentage change in sales over the previous year is given below.
2021: +10%
2022: −20%
2023: +25%
What were the company's sales in 2023?
questions.explanation:
Apply the changes one after another:
2021: 250 × 1.10 = 275.
2022: 275 × 0.80 = 220.
2023: 220 × 1.25 = 275.
Sales in 2023 = ₹275 crore. (Adding 10 − 20 + 25 = 15% to 250 gives the wrong value 287.5.)
